text: O VERDOSAGE The symptoms of overdosage of glycopyrrolate are peripheral in nature rather than central. To guard against further absorption of the drug–use gastric lavage, cathartics and/or enemas. To combat peripheral anticholinergic effects (residual mydriasis, dry mouth, etc.)–utilize a quaternary ammonium anticholinesterase, such as neostigmine methylsulfate. To combat hypotension–use pressor amines (norepinephrine, metaraminol) i.v.; and supportive care. To combat respiratory depression–administer oxygen; utilize a respiratory stimulant such as Dopram ® i.v.; artificial respiration.
